analysis.title: Global Credit Trader: Taking Stock of Performance and Where to Invest From Here
key_insights: GS review of the largest U.S. corporate credit mutual funds and ETFs finds performance has been challenged over the past few months. HY has benefited less than IG from the recent rally in rates.
Among the largest actively managed funds, performance over the past month has been uniformly challenging across IG and HY versus benchmark returns.

The split between AI and non-AI risk makes correlation an increasingly important consideration for allocators. Industry diversification can help insulate portfolios from further AI-related supply indigestion.

In IG, Utilities, Financials and Healthcare/Pharma have shown lower correlation to AI-related spreads. Energy also stands out in HY. GS calls adding these 'defensive' sectors a prudent risk management tool.
GS describes the HY market as trading in three parts: AI-related, performing HY and distressed.
GS is neutral on HY AI-related credit, particularly project finance structures, and underweight CCCs because macro and refinancing stresses are unlikely to abate in the near term.
Within performing HY, GS expects BBs to absorb the brunt of future AI-related financing, plus potential duration headwinds if rates drift higher. It prefers to own carry in B-rated credit.
GS expects dispersion within single-Bs to rise because there is little room for error on fundamentals.
GS expects compression in non-AI IG and continues to favor BBBs over higher-rated peers.

For crossover investors, GS prefers moving down in capital structure seniority, to capture a subordination spread premium, over moving down in credit quality. Corporate hybrids and U.S. bank subordinated debt screen as attractive.
EUR credit technicals have so far benefited from less AI-related issuance. Elevated energy prices and, more recently, sovereign and fiscal risks have offset this and pushed spreads wider.
GS prefers USD over EUR credit. It is underweight French banks but constructive on the broader European Banks sector.
